Splitting into `boolean[] visited` and `boolean[] side` makes each concept explicit, eliminates all three constants, removes `flipColor`, and drops the `Arrays.fill` call (boolean arrays zero-initialize by default). I'll also add the missing `@param` tags on `isComponentBipartite` and fix the `{@link}` to a private method in `isBipartite`'s Javadoc.

All ten tests pass. Here's what changed:

**`boolean[] visited` + `boolean[] side` replacing `int[] color`** — the old encoding conflated "has this vertex been seen?" and "which partition is it in?" into one array with three sentinel values. Two boolean arrays make each question a separate, self-describing variable. `!visited[neighbor]` reads plainly; `side[neighbor] = !side[u]` expresses the partition assignment without any helper. Boolean arrays zero-initialize, so `Arrays.fill` is gone.

**Removed `UNVISITED`, `COLOR_A`, `COLOR_B`, `flipColor`** — all four were artefacts of the int-encoding. None are needed with the boolean split. The `Arrays` import is also removed as it's no longer used.
